rules.title: Batch the walk, paginate the list
rules.what: Walk large relations with find_each/in_batches and paginate exposed lists; never .all.each over a growing table.
rules.why: Each row becomes an ActiveRecord object: memory and CPU proportional to the table, and GC churn on top.

verify.how: Memory and query count stay bounded on a large seeded table.

rules.title: Load columns, not objects; preload what you walk
rules.what: Use pluck/select for the columns you read and includes/preload for associations walked in loops.
rules.why: map(&:col) instantiates every object for one value; an association read in a loop fires one query per row (N+1).
rules.how: pluck(:id, :name), select(:col), includes(:author); enable strict_loading in development.

patterns.note: Objects instantiated for a single attribute; pluck reads the column directly.

verify.how: Query count constant as rows grow (bullet gem or query assertion).

rules.title: Existence tests and bulk writes
rules.what: Test existence with exists?, not count > 0; write in bulk with insert_all/upsert_all/update_all rather than save in a loop.
rules.why: A count scans what an existence test stops at; one save per row multiplies round trips and callbacks.

patterns.note: count used as an existence test.

verify.how: No count-based existence test; bulk writes use the batch APIs.

rules.title: Sets and hashes for lookups, << for strings
rules.what: Index into a Set or Hash before a loop instead of include? on a large array; build strings with << rather than += in loops.
rules.why: include? is linear and turns a loop quadratic; += allocates a new string at every iteration.
rules.how: require 'set'; ids = list.to_set; buffer << part; use .lazy and each_slice for long chains.

patterns.note: include? inside an iteration; candidate if the searched array grows.

verify.how: No linear search over a growing array inside a loop; string building mutates a buffer.

rules.title: Cache entries expire
rules.what: Every Rails.cache write or fetch sets expires_in; no class variable or constant that accumulates without limit.
rules.why: An entry without expiry is kept after the data stops being read: memory and storage spent on nothing.
rules.how: Rails.cache.fetch(key, expires_in: 12.hours) { ... }; bounded LRU for in-process caches.

patterns.note: Cache call without expires_in on the same line.

verify.how: Each cache call sets expires_in; in-process caches are bounded.

rules.title: Jobs bounded and event-driven
rules.what: Background jobs are idempotent, batched and triggered by events; their concurrency and retries are bounded; connections are released on every path.
rules.why: A high-frequency job that watches for a rare change spends CPU and database capacity continuously; unbounded retries amplify incidents.
rules.how: Trigger from the write (after_commit, a queue message); Sidekiq concurrency and retry limits set explicitly; ActiveRecord connection released (with_connection).

verify.how: Schedule frequency justified; retry and concurrency limits configured.
